introduction: On this Sunday, the Book of Wisdom tells us that God did not make death; he created all things to live. In the Gospel, Jesus heals a woman who has suffered for twelve years and raises the twelve-year-old daughter of Jairus. Paul asks the Corinthians to share generously, as Christ became poor for our sake. Let us bring our sick and our dead to the Lord of life.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, God did not make death; he delights in life. Let us pray to him for all in need.
intentions: For the Church: that she may bring Christ's healing touch to the sick and the suffering. Let us pray to the Lord.
For the sick, especially those with long or incurable illnesses: that they may find strength and healing in Christ. Let us pray to the Lord.
For parents whose children are ill, and for those who grieve a child: that Jesus may say to them, Do not be afraid, only believe. Let us pray to the Lord.
For the poor: that those who have much may share generously, as Christ became poor to make us rich. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may reach out to Jesus in faith, as the woman touched his cloak. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: God of life, you created us for incorruption and sent your Son to conquer death. Touch us with his healing, and raise us to new life in him. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Talitha cumi
reflection.body:
The Book of Wisdom makes a bold statement: "God didn't make death, neither does he delight when the living perish." God created all things to exist, and "God created man for incorruption." Death was not part of God's original plan.

The Gospel shows Jesus confronting sickness and death. Jairus, a leader of the synagogue, falls at his feet: "My little daughter is at the point of death." On the way to his house, a woman who has suffered from bleeding for twelve years, and spent everything she had on doctors, comes up behind Jesus in the crowd. She thinks, "If I just touch his clothes, I will be made well." She is healed at once. Jesus stops and looks for her, not to scold her but to give her more than a cure: "Daughter, your faith has made you well. Go in peace."

Then news comes that Jairus' daughter has died. Jesus says to him, "Don't be afraid, only believe." At the house he takes the girl by the hand and speaks to her in her own language: "Talitha cumi!" which means "Girl, I tell you, get up!" She gets up and walks, and Jesus, practical and tender, tells them to give her something to eat.

Both women were twelve years in their suffering or their life. Both were restored by Jesus' touch. The Church has always seen in these healings a sign of the Resurrection to come.

Paul applies the Gospel to money: "though he was rich, yet for your sakes he became poor, that you through his poverty might become rich." Generosity flows from that gift.

This week, bring to Jesus someone you know who is sick or grieving, and pray for them by name. And reach out yourself with faith, like the woman in the crowd: Jesus notices every hand that touches him.
